record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Suppose the Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = b(t)u(θ(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_θu)(t) is solved on a uniform mesh by collocation in the continuous piecewise-polynomial space S^{(0)}_m(I_h), with collocation points X_h as in (2.2) and initial value u_h(0) = g(0)/(1 - b(0)) under the assumption |b(t)| < 1 on I. Does the associated iterated collocation solution retain the optimal local superconvergence orders from Theorem 2.2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3 Suppose that the VFIE (1.3) is solved by collocation in the continuous piecewise polynomial space S(0) m (Ih), with uniform mesh Ih, collocation points Xh given in (2.2), and initial value uh(0) = g(0)/(1−b(0)) (assuming |b(t)| < 1 on I). Do the optimal local superconvergence orders of Theorem 2.2 remain valid for the iterated collocation associated with this uh?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I=[0,T]$ and consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation
$$u(t) = b(t)\,u(\theta(t)) + g(t) + (Vu)(t) + (V_\theta u)(t), \qquad t\in I,$$
where $b,g\in C(I)$ with $|b(t)|<1$ on $I$, the delay function $\theta:I\to I$ is continuous with $\theta(0)=0$ and $0\le\theta(t)<t$ for $t>0$ (a vanishing delay; the prototypical case is $\theta(t)=qt$ with $0<q<1$), and the Volterra operators are
$$(Vu)(t)=\int_0^t K(t,s)u(s)\,ds, \qquad (V_\theta u)(t)=\int_0^{\theta(t)} K_\theta(t,s)u(s)\,ds,$$
with sufficiently smooth kernels $K,K_\theta$.

Introduce a uniform mesh $I_h:\,0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$, $t_n=nh$, and the continuous piecewise polynomial space
$$S_m^{(0)}(I_h)=\{v\in C(I):\,v|_{[t_{n-1},t_n]}\in\Pi_m,\ n=1,\dots,N\}.$$
For prescribed collocation parameters $0<c_1<\cdots<c_m\le 1$, define the set of collocation points
$$X_h=\{t_{n-1}+c_i h:\ n=1,\dots,N,\ i=1,\dots,m\}.$$
The collocation solution $u_h\in S_m^{(0)}(I_h)$ is determined by the collocation equations
$$u_h(t)=b(t)u_h(\theta(t))+g(t)+(Vu_h)(t)+(V_\theta u_h)(t) \quad\text{for all }t\in X_h,$$
together with the initial condition $u_h(0)=g(0)/(1-b(0))$.

The iterated collocation solution is defined by
$$u_h^{it}(t):= b(t)u_h(\theta(t))+g(t)+(Vu_h)(t)+(V_\theta u_h)(t),\qquad t\in I.$$

Assume that for a suitable choice of the collocation parameters $\{c_i\}$ (e.g.\ Radau II or Gauss points), the collocation solution $u_h$ attains the known optimal local superconvergence orders at the mesh points (i.e.\ $\max_{0\le n\le N}|u(t_n)-u_h(t_n)|=O(h^{m+\kappa})$ for some $\kappa\ge 1$ characterizing the optimal local superconvergence).

Question: Does the iterated collocation solution $u_h^{it}$ retain these same optimal local superconvergence orders at the mesh points (and on $X_h$) as $u_h$, under the assumption $|b(t)|<1$ on $I$ and with the above initial value?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search indicates that superconvergence of collocation and iterated collocation methods for Volterra functional integral equations with vanishing/proportional delays remains an active research area (Brunner, Hu and collaborators), with results obtained for special meshes (geometric, quasi-geometric) and for certain delay structures. No source was found that explicitly resolves the specific question of whether the iterated collocation solution on uniform meshes in $S_m^{(0)}(I_h)$ retains the optimal local superconvergence orders under $|b(t)|<1$. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Optimal superconvergence results for Volterra functional integral equations with proportional vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a technique to study optimal convergence orders of collocation methods for VFIEs with vanishing delays on quasi-geometric meshes; superconvergence of order m+1 at nodes for Radau II points.
status_evidence.claim: Related superconvergence questions for VFIEs with vanishing delays continue to be investigated, but the iterated-collocation question on uniform meshes is not explicitly resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Geometric meshes in collocation methods for Volterra integral equations with proportional delays
status_evidence.snippet: Iterated piecewise polynomial collocation on geometric meshes leads to almost optimal superconvergence at mesh points for VIEs with proportional delays.
status_evidence.claim: Iterated collocation superconvergence is established on geometric (not uniform) meshes, leaving the uniform-mesh case for VFIEs open.
